why: THREE money channels, not one. They are funded differently, readable differently, and must not be gated by one number. Each floor below carries its PROVENANCE, because a custodian-stated limit and a number the executive invented are not the same kind of fact and must never be recorded as though they were.

openrouter.what: per-token, priced per call; what the rounds actually spend
openrouter.how_read: priced from the model table before the call; tools/round_cycle.py --budget

claude_subscription.what: prepaid monthly; funds Claude Code, i.e. the executive's own operation

floor.kind: percent of the seven-day window remaining
floor.provenance: NO FLOOR SET. The custodian has stated one for Codex and not for this channel. The executive declines to invent a number here: an invented floor recorded beside a stated one would be indistinguishable from it later.

codex_subscription.enforced_by: NOTHING IN CODE, standing. The custodian holds rate limiting for this channel directly, by monitoring weekly Claude Code and Codex usage. tools/codex_call.py still writes an invocation receipt for every call and persists every transcript; only the wall-clock gate is gone. Setting codex_call.RATE_LIMITING_HELD_BY to an empty string restores the floor.

floor.kind: held by the custodian, not by a tool
floor.provenance: custodian, 2026-08-11: 'Remove the Codex floor because I will monitor Claude Code and Codex usage for the 7-day period ending Monday August 17.' Made STANDING 2026-08-12: 'remove the codex floor because i will monitor the weekly usage.' The first instruction carried a stated window and this record refused to let it outlive that window silently; the second removes the window deliberately, which is a different fact and is recorded as one.
floor.why_removed: The floor was a wall-clock PROXY for a channel this policy records as unreadable. It was overridden on 18 of 21 invocations (86%). A control bypassed nine times in ten is a receipt, not a control.
what_this_does_not_establish: That any monitoring is happening. This record holds no artifact of it — no reading, no cadence, no threshold — and cannot distinguish a channel watched weekly from one nobody looks at. The control is real and it is OUTSIDE the record.

That the executive's Codex spend is bounded. Nothing here bounds it. What is bounded is the executive's ability to spend it UNRECORDED: every invocation writes a receipt and a transcript, so the custodian's monitoring has something to monitor.

That removing it was cheap. Codex review is the single most productive defect-finding mechanism this project has — on 2026-08-12 it found seven real defects across three rounds, every one past eight green gates. A floor on it is a floor on that.

rate_limit.provenance: UNMEASURED. The custodian said 'at least 10 minutes'; the custodian also holds the measurement of how fast Codex actually exhausts the weekly window, which is what the spacing should be derived from. Until that measurement is recorded here, 600 is a floor honoured, not a rate justified.
rate_limit.exemption: Moot while the floor is held by the custodian. Retained because the machinery returns if RATE_LIMITING_HELD_BY is cleared. Owner 2026-08-10: 'Ignore Codex rate limits when acting on my immediate direction.' Use --override with the direction as the reason.

what_this_does_not_establish: That the executive's own calls are counted. 23 of the 25 Codex invocations on 2026-08-09 were made directly through the shell before the wrapper existed, and are absent from the action log. The log undercounts by construction, not by accident.
That the Claude reading is fine-grained enough to derive a burn rate. Utilisation is reported as an integer percent and did not move across 2h41m of trial work.
